newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks eke out modest gains.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks eke out modest gains.

text.p: Colombian stocks eked out modest gains in a market that saw continuing demand for brewer Bavaria SA and strong buying of shares in Banco de Bogota, brokers said.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index rose 0.20 percent to close at 16,075.37 on a above-average volume of 3.5 billion pesos that was fueled by active cross-trading in shares of leading retailer Almancenes Exito.
Bogota's closed up 0.10 percent, meanwhile, ending the day at 1,030.82 on a lackluster volume of 1 billion pesos.
Brokers said demand for Bavaria, which has risen steadily in recent weeks and is one of the country's most liquid shares, remained strong although it was less noticeable than in previous sessions.
The brewing company, which is owned by the powerful Julio Maria Santo Domingo industrial group, moved up 0.75 percent in Medellin to close at 6,700 pesos per share.
Banco de Bogota, the country's third largest bank in terms of assets, led gainers as it moved up on buying sparked by market rumors of strong 1996 results.
The bank's shares rose 1.61 percent in Bogota, where it closed at 6,300 pesos per share, and 1.74 percent in Medellin, where it ended the week at 6,310.
Losers included blue-chip Banco Ganadero, which fell 0.31 percent in Bogota to end at 316 pesos per share, and Banco de Colombia, which edged down 0.23 percent to end at 419.
Brokers attributed the losses by Colombia's two biggest banks to a general lack of demand following their run-up earlier this year.
